analysis.evidence: מִשָּׁם marks the point of departure, “from there,” and הָהָרָה marks the destination, “to the hill country.” Abram then pitches his tent east of Bethel.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a third-person masculine singular Hiphil wayyiqtol. The subject is Abram.

draft.change: Explain the marked occurrence in the existing Genesis 12:8 evidence for the adverb at word index 1.
draft.definition: שָׁם points to a place identified in context. With מִן it designates the place from which someone or something moves.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:8 places מִשָּׁם after the verb of movement and before the destination הָהָרָה, yielding ‘from there toward the hill country’.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּעְתֵּק מִשָּׁם הָהָרָה, Abram moves from his previous location near Shechem toward the hill country. מִשָּׁם gives the point of departure and הָהָרָה gives the destination.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition מִן means ‘from’. Its נ assimilates to the following שׁ, producing the dagesh in שָּׁם. The second segment is the place adverb שָׁם, ‘there’.
analysis.sense: there, referring to the place Abram left

analysis.evidence: וַיַּעְתֵּק מִשָּׁם describes Abram moving from his previous campsite. The verse locates his new camp with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east, supporting the regional sense of the highland east of Bethel.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun. The final directional ־ָה marks the destination of Abram’s movement.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68354:2, 66328:4, 66056:5.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun with prefixed preposition מִן. The dagesh in ק marks assimilation of the נ.

analysis.evidence: מִקֶּדֶם לְבֵית אֵל locates Abram’s camp east of Bethel. The verse then places בֵּית אֵל to the west of the tent and Ai to the east. The full name identifies the town, and the marked word supplies its “house of” element.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ introduces the reference point for מִקֶּדֶם, yielding “east of.” בֵית is the masculine singular construct of בַּיִת, followed by אֵל as the second element of the place name.

analysis.evidence: In מִקֶּדֶם לְבֵית אֵל, “east of Bethel,” בֵית means “house of” and the marked אֵל supplies “God.” The verse later places בֵּית אֵל west of Abram’s tent and Ai to the east, confirming that the whole phrase names a place.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun completing the construct phrase בֵּית אֵל.

analysis.evidence: The direct object אָהֳלֹה, “his tent,” identifies what Abram spread out after moving to the hill country east of Bethel.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed וַ with the shortened Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּט אָהֳלֹה means “he pitched his tent.” The suffix refers to Abram, and the verse locates his tent between Bethel on the west and Ai on the east.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix, written ־ֹה.
